ea-gh-one-mediator.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does one Mediator leave the door wide open? Because the way to the Father is already opened by Jesus, the one Mediator, and the veil was torn from the top, by Yahweh Himself. So every added go-between, a teacher, a technique, an angel, adds something the Word says does not exist. It does not add help; it quietly says the Son is not quite enough. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-one-mediator.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does one Mediator leave the door wide open, and why does every shortcut add what Scripture never promised? Because the office is filled. Jesus gave Himself a ransom, the veil is torn, and He ever lives to make intercession for you. Angels refuse the role, and good teachers point past themselves to Him. So test every practice with one question: does this add a middleman? Then come boldly, in His name, with nothing to qualify for. You are already heard.

teen.open: Do you need someone or something extra to get through to Yahweh? No. There is one Mediator, Jesus, and through Him the door to the Father is already wide open.
teen.close: So you do not need a middleman. Jesus is the only go-between, and He is never too busy. Anything that says you must go through someone else adds what the Bible never promised. Just pray in His name.

senior.open: The title asks why one Mediator leaves the door wide open. The lesson's answer is that the office is already filled by the man Christ Jesus, and through Him every believer has direct access to the Father.
senior.close: So the question is answered. One Mediator means the way is open, the veil torn from the top, and the Son still interceding for us. Any practice that inserts another go-between adds what Scripture never promised. We may come boldly in His name, with nothing to earn first.

Because Yahweh is love, the one who dwells in love dwells in Him, and He in him (1 John 4:16). A heart that lives there re-warms, lets perfect love cast out its fear, and carries that warmth to others. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-inside-love.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could a cold world be warmed from the inside? Yes, one heart at a time. The love of many grows cold, and hearts armor up to survive. But Yahweh is love, His love was proved at the cross, and the Holy Ghost pours it into our hearts. When you believe that love and move your address into it, fear loses its grip and the armor comes off. Then the love you live in becomes the love you give, warmth in a cold place.

teen.open: Can a heart that has gone cold get warm again? Yes. Not by forcing feelings, but by living inside Yahweh's love, because Yahweh is love.
teen.close: So a cold world can be warmed from the inside. Believe Yahweh loves you, live in His love like a home, let it push out fear, and then pass that love on to the people around you.

senior.open: The title asks whether a cold world could be warmed from the inside. First John 4:16 answers yes: since Yahweh is love, to dwell in love is to dwell in Him, and a heart that lives there is warmed by where it lives.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. The warmth does not come from effort but from relocation into His everlasting love. There perfect love casts out fear, and the love we receive flows out to others, even where the love of many has grown cold.

Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-whole-spirit-soul-body.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Should you split yourself into parts, or let the Word divide? Let the Word do the dividing, and let Yahweh do the keeping. You are one person, made by Him and kept by Him: spirit, soul and body together. Reading is the instrument, not introspection. teen.open: Do you have to sort out and fight against parts of yourself? No. Yahweh keeps all of you, spirit, soul and body, and His Word does the dividing, not your own inner searching.
teen.close: So you do not have to split yourself up or treat your body like an enemy. Read His Word and let it sort things out. Yahweh keeps the whole you, and resting and eating are part of how He cares for you.

senior.open: The title asks whether to split ourselves into parts or let the Word divide. The lesson answers plainly: Yahweh keeps the whole person, spirit and soul and body, and the dividing of soul from spirit belongs to His Word, not to our own introspection.
senior.close: So the answer holds. We are not asked to rank or override our parts. The Word divides, Yahweh keeps, and a weary body is cared for, as Elijah was, not condemned. He who calls us is faithful, and He will raise and keep the whole of us.

ea-gh-die-daily.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could you be ready to go Home any day? Yes, if you die daily. Each morning you put the old self down before it runs the day: your preferences, your offense, your right to yourself. You keep short accounts and live as a traveler, because this is not Home. When the dying is already done today, going Home holds no terror. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-die-daily.example: ONE ORDINARY MORNING. Say you wake up still stung by a sharp word from yesterday. The old man wants to carry it into the day. Dying daily looks like this: you lay the offense down in prayer, you call and say I am sorry for your part, you tell your family I love you before you leave. Small things. But if the call came that night, there would be nothing left to settle.
ea-gh-die-daily.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could you be ready to go Home any day? Yes. That is what Paul's I die daily and Jesus' take up your cross daily ask of you each morning: lay down the old self before he takes the wheel, forgive and confess today, and hold this life loosely as a pilgrim. Each surrender is a seed that falls and bears fruit. Christ has broken the fear of death, so readiness becomes a way of life, and when the call comes, you simply go Home.

teen.open: Could you be ready to meet Jesus any day? Yes. Every morning you give Him the old you, the part that wants its own way, and you live knowing this world is not your final home.
teen.close: So readiness is a daily habit. Each morning, let go of your own way, forgive quickly, say sorry and I love you today. Then you have nothing to fear, because Jesus has gone ahead to prepare a place.

senior.open: The title asks whether you could be ready to go Home any day. The lesson's answer is yes, by dying daily: each morning laying down the old self before it runs the day, and living as a pilgrim whose Home is ahead.
senior.close: So the question is answered. Readiness is not a last-minute scramble but a way of life: the self surrendered each morning, short accounts kept, and death faced without terror because Christ has broken its bondage. Then, like Paul, we can say we are ready.

ea-gh-spirit-bears-witness-with.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your gut feeling the final witness? teen.open: Is your gut feeling the final proof that you belong to Yahweh? No. His Spirit and your spirit both testify, and His is the one that settles it.
teen.close: So do not trust your feelings as the last word. Go to His Word and His Spirit, and let your heart agree. Even on a bad day, you are still His child, sealed by the Holy Spirit.

senior.open: The title asks whether your inner feeling is the final witness of your sonship. Romans 8:16 says there are two witnesses, His Spirit with ours, and the confirming testimony belongs to His Spirit, not to our changing inner state.
senior.close: So the answer is no. Our spirit is a witness that recognises and confirms, not an oracle. Because the final testimony is His, our assurance survives grief, illness and low moods. We are adopted, sealed, and kept, and nothing can separate us from His love.

ea-gh-confess-believe.example: ONE SENTENCE, TWO HEARERS. Say a coworker asks you why you follow Jesus. You do not need a lecture. You can say: I confessed that Jesus is Lord, I believe Yahweh raised Him from the dead, and He saved me. That is your mouth and your heart agreeing out loud. And the same sentence shows your coworker the way: the word is near them too, in their mouth and in their heart.
ea-gh-confess-believe.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How does Romans 10:9 make salvation clear enough to live and share? By putting your mouth and your heart on the same team. The heart believes Yahweh raised Jesus; the mouth confesses Jesus is Lord; and the promise is a certainty for whosoever, Jew or Greek, thief or jailer. You can rest in it, because John wrote so you may know. And because faith comes by hearing, you open your mouth again. Someone told you. Now you tell someone.

teen.open: How simple is it to be saved? Romans 10:9 says to say with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that Yahweh raised Him from the dead. Then you shall be saved.
teen.close: So your mouth and heart work together. Believe Jesus rose, say He is Lord, and you are saved, for sure. It is simple enough to tell a friend in one sentence, so tell someone.

senior.open: The title says the mouth and the heart are on the same team. Romans 10:9 shows how: the heart believes Yahweh raised Jesus from the dead, the mouth confesses Him as Lord, and the promise is stated as a certainty.
senior.close: So the answer is clear. Salvation joins heart and mouth, rests on a promise that cannot fail, and is open to whosoever calls. Because faith comes by hearing, the one who has confessed is also sent to tell the next person.

ea-gh-renew-mind.reason: Explains conformed versus transformed and neuroplasticity first; the plain answer (the world presses its mold on an unrenewed mind; feed the Word, starve the conforming feeds, then prove His will) is gathered only in WHAT CHANGES.
ea-gh-renew-mind.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your mind running someone else's program? It is if it is conformed to this world, pressed into the world's mold of values, fears and appetites. Romans 12:2 gives the way out: surrender yourself to Yahweh, then be transformed by the renewing of your mind, feeding on the Word and starving the feeds that press you back into the mold. A renewed mind stops guessing at His will and starts proving it, testing it and finding it good. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-renew-mind.example: ONE EVENING, TWO FEEDS. Say most nights you scroll for an hour before bed, and most mornings you wake anxious and comparing. That is the world's mold being poured in. Now say you trade half that hour for a psalm read slowly and turned over in your mind. What you feed grows; what you starve weakens. Weeks later, the anxious default has a rival, and the Word is shaping what you notice and choose.
ea-gh-renew-mind.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your mind running someone else's program? Not once it is being renewed. The world presses from outside, but transformation works from within. You present yourself to Yahweh first, then feed on His Word day and night and starve the feeds that conform you, repeated until the mind of Christ is your default. Then His will stops being a mystery. You test it by doing it, and you prove in your own life that it is good, acceptable and perfect.

teen.open: Is your mind just copying what the world tells you to want and fear? Romans 12:2 says do not be pressed into the world's shape. Let Yahweh change your thinking from the inside.
teen.close: So you can take your mind back. Give yourself to Yahweh, feed on His Word every day, and cut back what pushes you into the world's mold. Then you will see for yourself that His way is good.

senior.open: The title asks whether your mind is running someone else's program. Romans 12:2 answers that the world is always pressing us into its mold, and that the remedy is transformation by the renewing of the mind, so that we may prove Yahweh's will.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Surrender comes first, then daily renewal: the Word fed in, the conforming influences starved. Over time the mind of Christ becomes our habit, and His will is no longer guessed at but proved good, acceptable and perfect.

ea-gh-truth-love.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why can the same honest words heal or hurt? Because truth lands by relationship and framing, not only by accuracy. Heard from a trusted friend and offered as care, a hard truth heals; thrown as a weapon, the same truth makes a person armor up. The answer is truth in love, like a mirror that shows what is there without mocking or condemning, so the person can see and be free. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-truth-love.example: ONE TRUTH, TWO DELIVERIES. Say a friend has been short with his children. One person says it in front of others, with a sigh: you are always angry. He bristles and defends himself. Another person, who has dealt with her own temper first, waits for a quiet moment and says: I love your family, and I noticed the kids go quiet when you are tired. Same truth. The second one is a mirror, and he can look into it.
ea-gh-truth-love.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why can the same honest words heal or hurt? Because truth is received through relationship. Jesus was full of grace and truth, and Nathan built a mirror before he pointed into it, so David broke and was restored. So before you speak, check your love and your own beam; before you flinch, check whether a friend is wounding you faithfully. Truth offered as care grows a person. Be that mirror, and the truth sets people free.

teen.open: Why does a true thing sometimes help and sometimes sting? It depends on how it is said and who says it. Truth spoken in love helps; truth thrown like a rock hurts.
teen.close: So be like a mirror. Tell the truth kindly, at the right time, after checking your own heart. And when a friend tells you something hard, listen instead of fighting back. That is how truth sets people free.

senior.open: The title asks why the same honest words can heal or hurt. The lesson's answer is that truth is received through relationship and framing: offered in love, it heals; thrown as a weapon, it hardens.
senior.close: So the answer stands. Like Nathan before David, we build the mirror before we point into it, speaking with grace and good timing, and we receive faithful wounds from friends with humility. Truth in love is how people grow and are set free.

ea-gh-kenosis.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What path does Yahweh use to lift Jesus? Down first. The Son came off the throne, emptied Himself by taking the form of a servant, took a towel, and went all the way to the cross in obedience. Wherefore the Father highly exalted Him and gave Him the Name above every name. Down is the way up. And the same mind is to be in you: step down in obedience and service, secure in Him, and let the Father lift you on His timing and terms.

teen.close: So the path up is down. Jesus left His throne, served, and died on the cross, and then the Father lifted Him higher than everyone. When you choose to serve and step down, you are walking His path, and the Father lifts you in His time.

senior.close: So the question is answered. The path Yahweh used to lift Jesus was descent in obedience, all the way to the cross, and then exaltation to the Name above every name. That same mind is ours to share, stepping down and serving, and leaving the lifting to the Father.

ea-gh-church-born-fire.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does Peter say about a people whose worth Yahweh fixed? That the price sets the worth, and the price was the precious Blood of Christ, not silver or gold. No market, no nation's ledger, no balcony, back row or law against reading can mark that price down. A church born in exclusion still thrives by following Yahweh, and every kindred and nation will stand before the Lamb. So refuse every price tag the world puts on you or anyone else, and live as a royal priest, showing forth His praises.

teen.close: So what are you worth? The world prices people by skin, money or family name, but Yahweh paid for His people with the Blood of Jesus. Nothing costs more, and nobody can mark that price down. Treat yourself and others that way.

senior.close: So the question is answered. Our worth was fixed by the price Yahweh paid, the precious Blood of Christ, and no nation or market can reprice it. The church born in that fire still thrives by obedience, and every nation redeemed by the same Blood will stand before the same throne.

The Word teaches that Christ is before all things and holds them together, so His Word is the highest-priority code. When anything conflicts with it, that thought is preempted, not merged. Decide that in advance, and every thought can be brought captive to the obedience of Christ. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-higher-priority.example: ONE HEADLINE, ALREADY DECIDED. Say you read a story that sets off a wave of fear about the future. Without a decision made ahead of time, you argue with that fear all evening. With the decision made, the case is already closed: the Word wins every conflict. You answer the fear with what is written, as Jesus did in the wilderness (Matthew 4:4), and think on what is true (Philippians 4:8). The fear does not get a new trial.
ea-gh-higher-priority.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Which program runs your mind? The one you let run first, and the Word says it must be the King's. Christ is before all things, by Him all things consist, and He has the preeminence, so His Word outranks every headline, feed, fear and philosophy. Settle it in advance, the way Jesus answered every temptation with it is written. Feed on His words, which are spirit and life, and you will know the peace of a mind stayed on Him.

teen.open: Lots of voices fight for your attention every day. Which one gets to go first in your head? Paul says Jesus' Word gets top priority, over every other thought.
teen.close: So decide ahead of time: the Word wins. When a thought fights against what Yahweh says, you do not have to argue it out again. Answer it with Scripture, like Jesus did, and enjoy a calmer mind.

senior.open: The title asks which program runs your mind. Paul's answer is that every thought must be brought into captivity to Christ, because He is before all things and holds all things together, so His Word takes priority over every other voice.
senior.close: So the answer is settled. When we decide beforehand that the Word wins every conflict, we stop relitigating the same fears and opinions. We feed on His words daily, answer temptation with what is written, and find the perfect peace of a mind stayed on Him.

Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-quickened.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why did your heart need more than repair? Because it was dead, and the dead need life from outside themselves. Like dry bones or Lazarus in the tomb, we could contribute nothing. So Yahweh, rich in mercy, quickened us with Christ, gave a new heart and a new spirit, paid for it with the precious Blood of the Lamb, and adopted us in the same act. teen.open: Can you fix your own heart by trying harder? The Bible says no, because without Jesus we were dead in sin. Yahweh does not patch an old heart. He gives a brand new one.
teen.close: So your heart needed more than a fix. It needed new life, and Jesus paid for it with His Blood. You did not earn it; it is a gift. Now you get to live thankful and new.

senior.open: The title speaks of a heart that needed more than repair. Ephesians 2:1 explains why: we were dead in trespasses and sins, and so Yahweh promised through Ezekiel not to mend the stony heart but to replace it with a new heart and a new spirit.
senior.close: So the question is answered. The heart needed resurrection, not repair, and Yahweh gave it freely, bought with the Blood of Christ and joined to our adoption as His children. We no longer strive to patch the old self; we walk thankfully in newness of life.

ea-gh-resist-flee.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the adversary run when you stand in the right order? Because the authority to resist comes from being under authority. teen.open: Why does the enemy back off when you follow James 4:7? Because you submit to Yahweh first, then resist. Being under His authority is what gives your no its power.
teen.close: So the order matters. Give yourself to Yahweh first, then fight temptation with His Word, and run from what traps you. When you come close to Yahweh, He comes close to you.

senior.open: The title asks why the adversary flees when we stand in the right order. James answers that submission to Yahweh comes first and powers the resistance; resistance made from under His authority, with His Word, is what sends the enemy away.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Submitted resistance prevails, as it did for Jesus in the wilderness, while borrowed words without relationship fail. We humble ourselves, resist steadfast in the faith, flee what tempts us, and draw near to Yahweh, who draws near to us.

Your case has already been claimed by a higher Court that cannot be bribed, cannot be fooled and never forgets the evidence. That is why you can let go of revenge: dropping the case is not calling the wrong fine, it is handing it to the only Judge who will get it exactly right. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-vengeance-his.example: TWO EVENINGS AFTER ONE WRONG. Say a coworker takes credit for your work. One evening you replay it, draft the comeback, and wake up hurt all over again. Another evening you pray: Father, You hold this case; I hand it to You. Then you pray for him. The next day you still tell the truth plainly where it is needed, but you no longer rehearse the wound. The case is in a higher court, and your head is free.
ea-gh-vengeance-his.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who holds the score when you have been wronged? Yahweh, from the Law to the letters. David let Saul go, Joseph fed the brothers who sold him, and Jesus committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously. You can do the same, because you are eternal and your losses here are small beside what is kept for you, and because you have been forgiven far more. So stop rehearsing the wound, pray for the one who hurt you, overcome evil with good, and rest. The Judge never misses a case.

teen.open: When someone hurts you, who gets to settle it? Yahweh does. He says vengeance is His, so you do not have to get even.
teen.close: So you can let it go. Hand the hurt to Yahweh, the perfect Judge, pray for the person, and do good instead of getting even. Jesus forgave you, and He will handle what is fair.

senior.open: The title asks who holds the score when we are wronged. Romans 12:19 answers that vengeance belongs to Yahweh; He will repay, and so we are free to set down the case rather than try it ourselves.
senior.close: So the answer stands. The score is kept by a Judge who cannot be bribed or fooled. Like Joseph and David, and above all like Jesus, we entrust justice to Him, forgive as we have been forgiven, and overcome evil with good.

Happiness rises and falls with the forecast; the joy of the LORD is a strength you receive (Nehemiah 8:10), and it holds while circumstances swing. And the storm is not wasted: Yahweh uses testing as training, so those exercised by it come out stronger. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-good-fight-exercise.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What is your anchor when the storm hits? The joy of Yahweh, which is your strength. Habakkuk rejoiced with an empty barn; Paul and Silas sang at midnight in stocks; Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before Him. Trials are not pleasant, but they work patience, and the hard season becomes exercise that yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness. So you stop waiting for happiness before you can stand. You count it all joy, because the anchor holds and the fight is training you.

teen.open: Happiness comes and goes like the weather. So what keeps you steady in hard times? Joy in Yahweh, because it does not depend on how your day is going.
teen.close: So your anchor is joy in Yahweh, not good feelings. Hard times hurt, but He uses them to make you stronger. Like Paul and Silas singing in jail, you can stand and even sing, because He holds you.

senior.open: The title calls happiness weather and asks what anchors us in the storm. The lesson answers that joy indexed to Yahweh is that anchor, and that He uses the hard seasons as training for those exercised by them.
senior.close: So the answer is clear. Happiness follows circumstances, but the joy of the LORD is our strength and holds through loss. Trials work patience and, received as training, yield the peaceable fruit of righteousness. Seeking counsel and care along the way is part of fighting well.

ea-gh-seated-heavenly.reason: Opens on the finished tense of the seating, but what it means for the everyday walk (live from the seat, not toward it, and carry each other's burdens while we grow) only comes in the later sections.
ea-gh-seated-heavenly.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What do Ephesians 2:6 and Galatians 6:2 mean for your everyday walk? Two things. First, you are already seated with Christ in heavenly places, His finished act, so you live from that seat in rest instead of striving toward it. Second, you are still growing, and the growing is done together: because no one has to prove their place, everyone is free to carry someone else's burden. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-seated-heavenly.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does being already seated, still growing, mean for your everyday walk? It means your identity does not wobble with circumstances. Yahweh has raised you, seated you with Christ and blessed you with all spiritual blessings, and nothing can separate you from His love. So you stop striving to earn a place you already have, set your mind on things above, and come boldly to the throne for grace. Then you spend that freed energy beside a struggling brother or sister, bearing one another's burdens while we grow.

teen.open: What does it mean that you are already seated with Christ? It means your place with Yahweh is settled now. You are still growing, and you grow by helping each other.
teen.close: So you do not have to earn your spot with Yahweh. It is already yours. Live from that peace, and use your energy to help a friend carry what is heavy. That is how we grow together.

senior.open: The title says we are already seated and still growing. Ephesians 2:6 tells us the seating is Yahweh's finished act, and Galatians 6:2 shows the growing is done together, by bearing one another's burdens.
senior.close: So the question is answered. Because our seat with Christ is secure, we live from rest rather than striving, and that freedom is spent on others. The seated believer is not above the struggling one but beside him, helping him up.

ea-gh-confess-cleanse.reason: Opens with a long run of 1 John 1:5 to 2:2; the plain answer (confess, agree with Yahweh, and His faithfulness and the paid price fix the response: forgiven and cleansed) comes in sections two to four.
ea-gh-confess-cleanse.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could your mess be cleaned up today? Yes. If you confess, which means agreeing with Yahweh about what you did and naming it as He names it, He is faithful and just to forgive your sins and cleanse you from all unrighteousness (1 John 1:9). It works because of who He is: faithful keeps His word, and just means the price is already paid by Jesus. The response is fixed, so it is safe to come today. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-confess-cleanse.example: ONE SHARP WORD, CONFESSED THE SAME DAY. Say you snapped at your spouse this morning and have felt it all afternoon. Hiding it means carrying it, the way David said his bones waxed old while he kept silent. Confessing it is fast and specific: Father, I spoke in anger and wounded her; I agree with You it was sin. He forgives and cleanses. Then you tell her the same thing, and you pray together. By evening, it is settled.
ea-gh-confess-cleanse.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could your mess be cleaned up today? Yes, today. When you confess, you are not bargaining with a reluctant judge. Yahweh is faithful, and He is just because Jesus, our Advocate, already paid. He forgives the guilt and cleanses the stain, as far as the east is from the west. Hiding sin only lets it fester, as David learned; naming it fast and specifically brings it into the light. Like the prodigal's father, He runs to meet you. A clean slate is one honest prayer away.

teen.open: Can a mess you made be cleaned up today? Yes. When you tell Yahweh honestly what you did, He promises to forgive you and make you clean, because Jesus already paid.
teen.close: So do not hide it. Name what you did, quickly and honestly, and trust Yahweh to keep His promise. He forgives and cleans you up, today. Then say sorry to anyone you hurt, too.

senior.open: The title asks whether a mess could be cleaned up today. First John 1:9 answers yes: when we confess, agreeing with Yahweh about our sin, He is faithful and just to forgive and to cleanse, because the price has been paid by the Son.
senior.close: So the answer is certain. Confession works because it rests on His faithfulness and on the Blood, not on our performance. Hidden sin festers, as David found; confessed sin is forgiven and its stain removed. We may come quickly and specifically, and leave clean.

ea-gh-sow-bountifully.reason: States the sowing law early, but what the harvest actually is (grace and sufficiency to keep giving, not personal luxury) and the cheerful, purposed heart come in sections three and four.
ea-gh-sow-bountifully.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Sow little, reap little? Yes, Paul says the harvest matches the sowing (2 Corinthians 9:6). But read what he says the harvest is: grace abounding, sufficiency in all things so you can keep giving, the fruits of righteousness, and thanksgiving to Yahweh, not a formula for personal luxury. And the heart matters as much as the amount: purpose it ahead of time, and give cheerfully, not grudgingly or under pressure. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-sow-bountifully.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Sow little, reap little? Yes, and sow bountifully, reap bountifully. The harvest Yahweh gives is real: all grace, all sufficiency, every good work, fruits of righteousness and many thanksgivings. So decide in your heart ahead of time, and give cheerfully, the way the Macedonians gave out of deep poverty after first giving themselves to the Lord. Sow mercy, time and encouragement as well as money. You give because Jesus became poor for you, and Yahweh loves a cheerful giver.

teen.open: Does how much you give really matter? Paul says the harvest matches the sowing. And Yahweh cares about your heart: give on purpose, and give happily, not because you feel forced.
teen.close: So plan your giving, and give with a glad heart. It is not about getting rich. Yahweh gives you enough to keep giving and grows good fruit in you. You can give time and kindness too.

senior.open: The title asks whether sowing little means reaping little. Paul says it does, but he defines the harvest as grace and sufficiency for every good work, and he asks that giving be purposed in the heart and offered cheerfully.
senior.close: So the answer stands. We reap as we sow, and the harvest is grace, sufficiency, righteousness and thanksgiving to Yahweh. Purposed, cheerful giving, of money, mercy and time, trains the heart to trust a generous Father and honours the Son who became poor for us.

ea-gh-tested-soul.reason: Opens with long 1 Peter and James passages; the why (the fire refines and proves faith like gold, testing is universal, and it works patience toward a crown) is spread across sections three to seven.
ea-gh-tested-soul.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Yahweh let every believer be tested? Because testing refines faith the way fire refines gold: it does not destroy it, it proves it genuine and burns off the dross (1 Peter 1:7). He tests to strengthen, never to tempt toward evil. Every believer gets a turn, so a trial is not a sign He has left you. And beyond the fire waits the crown of life He promised to those who love Him (James 1:12). Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-tested-soul.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does Yahweh let every believer be tested? Because tested faith is the only kind you can trust under load. The Refiner sits over the fire, knows exactly how hot and how long, and never leaves the gold in a moment longer than needed. The trial works patience, experience and hope, and like Job you come forth as gold. So stop reading trials as abandonment, resist the temptation inside the test, and suffer like someone who knows: the crown of life is on the other side.

teen.open: Why does Yahweh let hard tests come to every believer? Because tests are like fire on gold. They do not wreck your faith; they make it pure and strong.
teen.close: So a hard test does not mean Yahweh left you. Everyone goes through it, and He is watching the whole time. Keep trusting Him, and you will come out like gold, with a crown of life waiting.

senior.open: The title asks why Yahweh lets every believer be tested. Peter and James answer that faith tried by fire is refined like gold and proved genuine, and that the one who endures receives the crown of life.
senior.close: So the question is answered. Testing is universal, purposeful and limited by a Refiner who watches closely. It produces patience and hope and proves our faith unto praise at Christ's appearing. We may suffer as those who know a crown waits beyond the fire.

ea-gh-clearly-seen-without-excuse.reason: Answers in the opening (the verdict falls not on ignorance but on withheld honor and thanks), and WHAT CHANGES restates it, but the lesson ends on a family-talk prompt instead of the answer.
ea-gh-clearly-seen-without-excuse.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why is ignoring the Designer the real blind spot? Because the evidence was never missing. The heavens declare His glory, and rain and fruitful seasons are His signature in every culture, so no one is without excuse. The blindness comes from what people do with it: knowing Him and not glorifying Him, admiring the work and passing over the Workman, until the foolish heart is darkened. The cure is simple and daily. Name Him, thank Him out loud, and give the glory back, and your mind stays lit.

teen.close: So the real blind spot is not missing proof. Yahweh's fingerprints are everywhere. It is seeing His work and not thanking Him. Name Him and say thanks for what you see, every day.

senior.close: So the answer is plain. Creation testifies clearly, and the failure Paul names is withheld honour and thanks, which darkens the heart. The remedy is to give Yahweh the glory openly and to keep giving thanks in everything.

ea-gh-assembling.reason: Opens on Hebrews 10:19-25; the answer to whether your absence matters (yes: you are a member of one Body, others need you and you them, more as the day nears) builds over the middle sections.
ea-gh-assembling.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does your absence make a difference? Yes. Believers are not a crowd of individuals but one Body, and every member needs the others. The gathering is where we consider one another, stir each other to love and good works, and carry each other's burdens. When you are missing, someone goes unencouraged, and you lose the strength you may need later. And Hebrews says to gather so much the more as the day approaches. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-assembling.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does your absence make a difference? It does. The eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of thee. Every joint supplies something, and when one member suffers, all suffer with it. Some weeks you will carry; other weeks you will be carried, and connections that were never formed cannot hold you then. So come ready to consider others, not only to receive. Gather more, not less, as the pressure grows, and Jesus is in the midst of you.

teen.open: Does it matter if you skip being with other believers? Yes. You are part of one body, and the others need what you bring, just like you need them.
teen.close: So show up. Your church family needs you, and some day you will need them. Go ready to encourage someone, and keep going, especially when life gets hard.

senior.open: The title asks whether your absence makes a difference. Hebrews 10:24-25 and Paul's picture of the Body answer yes: each member supplies something the others need, and the gathering is how the Body stays alive.
senior.close: So the answer holds. We are members one of another, and our presence encourages, strengthens and carries others, as theirs does for us. The Word asks us to gather all the more as the day draws near.

ea-gh-wages-and-gift.reason: Opens with Romans 6:16-23; the plain answer (death is the wage sin earns; eternal life is a gift received through Jesus, never earned) is given in the TWO LEDGERS and later sections.
ea-gh-wages-and-gift.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Earned wages or free gift? Both are in Romans 6:23, on two different ledgers. Death is the wage sin earns: what we have coming, and every one of us has it coming. Eternal life is the opposite: a gift from Yahweh, not earned, not owed, not deserved, and it comes only through Jesus Christ our Lord. You cannot pay the debt, so He hands you the life anyway. You only receive it. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-wages-and-gift.example: A PAYCHECK AND A PRESENT. Think of the difference at the end of a work week. A paycheck is owed; you earned it, and you would be right to complain if it did not come. A present on your birthday is not owed at all; you simply take it and say thank you. Sin works like the paycheck. Eternal life works like the present. Trying to earn it would turn it back into wages, and wages are not what any of us want.
ea-gh-wages-and-gift.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Earned wages or free gift? The wage of sin is real, and it is death; no one is exempt. But the gift of Yahweh is eternal life through Jesus, given while we were yet sinners, to the very ones who could never pay. So you take the wage seriously, and you stop trying to earn what is free. Receive the Son, because the life is in Him. Then live grateful, not entitled, and hand the same gift to others as freely as it was handed to you.

teen.open: Is eternal life something you earn or something you are given? Romans 6:23 says sin earns death, but eternal life is a free gift through Jesus.
teen.close: So you cannot earn it, and you do not have to. Sin's pay is death, but Yahweh gives life for free through Jesus. Receive Him, say thanks, and share that gift with others.

senior.open: The title sets earned wages beside a free gift. Romans 6:23 keeps the two ledgers separate: death is the wage sin earns, and eternal life is Yahweh's gift through Jesus Christ, which can only be received.
senior.close: So the answer is clear. The wage is real and the gift is free. We neither treat sin lightly nor strive to earn salvation. We receive the Son, in whom the life is, and live gratefully and generously.

ea-gh-god-of-this-world.reason: Opens on 2 Corinthians 4, John 8 and 1 John 5; the plain answer (the world is occupied, not neutral; a usurper blinds the default, and only the Light of Christ un-blinds) is stated in sections two to four.
ea-gh-god-of-this-world.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who is really steering the default? Not a neutral middle. When humanity walked out on its Maker, a usurper took the wheel: Paul calls him the god of this world, lowercase, and says he blinds the minds of those who do not believe (2 Corinthians 4:4). So the default is captivity, not neutrality, and good intentions alone do not free anyone. Only the Light of Christ opens blinded eyes. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-god-of-this-world.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who is really steering the default? The usurper, the father of lies, for every life still walking according to the course of this world. That is the blindness most people never notice. But Yahweh, rich in mercy, shines into the heart, and Jesus is the Light of the world. He delivers us from the power of darkness and carries us into the Kingdom of His dear Son. So stop treating the world as neutral, pray for blinded friends, keep coming to the Light, and choose your Father on purpose.

teen.open: Who is really in charge of the way the world normally goes? The Bible says the world is not neutral. The enemy, the god of this world, blinds people so they cannot see Jesus.
teen.close: So going along with the crowd is not a safe middle. Jesus is the Light who opens blind eyes and brings you into His Kingdom. Follow Him on purpose, and pray for friends who cannot see yet.

senior.open: The title asks who is really steering the default. Paul answers that the world is occupied, not neutral: the god of this world, a usurper, blinds unbelieving minds so the light of the gospel does not shine to them.
senior.close: So the answer is sobering and hopeful. The default is blindness, but the Light of Christ still shines and still opens eyes. We pray for the blinded rather than despise them, and we choose each day to live as children of the Father.

ea-gh-angels-left-their-estate.reason: The sentence on the fallen angels is shown early, but the courage the title promises (they are chained to a fixed end, judged at the cross, so you fight from victory) only arrives in the last sections.
ea-gh-angels-left-their-estate.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What do Jude 6 and 2 Peter 2:4 reveal, and what courage can you stand on? The angels who left their first estate are already sentenced: held in chains of darkness, reserved for the judgment of the great day. Jesus declared the verdict at the cross, when the prince of this world was judged. So the war is real, but it is not even. You resist from victory, not for it. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-angels-left-their-estate.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What courage can you stand on? A verdict already rendered. The rebels left the place their Creator gave them, and they are on a chain and a clock, with an end prepared for them. At the cross Christ spoiled principalities and powers and made a show of them openly. The roaring lion is still dangerous, so stay sober and wear the armor He supplies. But you do not fight in panic. You submit to Yahweh, resist from victory, and rejoice most that your name is written in heaven.

teen.open: Should you be scared of the enemy? Jude and Peter say the angels who rebelled are already sentenced and waiting for judgment. Jesus already won.
teen.close: So be careful, but do not be afraid. The enemy is a defeated prisoner, and Jesus is the Judge. Stay close to Yahweh, use His Word, and remember your name is written in heaven.

senior.open: The title speaks of courage drawn from a sentence already passed. Jude and Peter show that the angels who left their estate are reserved in chains for judgment, and Jesus declared at the cross that the prince of this world is judged.
senior.close: So the answer gives real courage. We take the battle seriously, yet we do not fear its outcome, because the enemy is condemned and we serve the Judge. We submit, resist from victory, keep the place He has given us, and rejoice that our names are written in heaven.

ea-gh-handling-word-deceitfully.reason: The opening states the answer (the Word can be held and handled deceitfully to say what He never meant), and WHAT CHANGES lands it, but the lesson ends on a family-talk prompt.
ea-gh-handling-word-deceitfully.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is holding the Bible the same as being changed by it? No. The Pharisees knew the Scriptures and used Corban to escape honoring their parents; the tempter quoted a psalm to push Jesus toward presumption; the unstable wrest Paul's letters to their own destruction. Possessing is not submitting. So rightly divide the Word: read in context, let it explain itself, and read for His will, not for permission. And watch what you do when it corrects you. The honest reader lets the Word win.

teen.close: So knowing Bible verses is not the same as obeying them. Do not use Scripture to win arguments or excuse yourself. Read it carefully, let it correct you, and do what it says.

senior.close: So the answer is plain. Scripture can be quoted to defend our own ways, as the Corban tradition did, and that harms the one who twists it. The faithful reader rightly divides the Word, reads for Yahweh's will, and lets it judge and correct him.

ea-gh-friendship-world-enmity.reason: Answers early (no neutral middle; love people, not the world-system), but ends on discussion prompts after WHAT CHANGES, so the reader does not finish on the answer.
ea-gh-friendship-world-enmity.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you be close to the world and still close to Yahweh? Not to the world-system. James calls friendship with it spiritual adultery, and John says the love of the Father is not in the one who loves it. You can live among people, love them, work and build in the middle of them, and still keep your love undivided. Here is how the Word draws that line.
ea-gh-friendship-world-enmity.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you be close to the world and still close to Yahweh? You can be in the world, among people He loves, but you cannot be a friend of the world-system and His friend at the same time. There is no neutral middle; the choice is made in the particulars your affection holds onto. The way back is not trying harder but drawing near in humility, because He gives more grace. And the payoff is lasting: the world passes away, but the one who does His will abides for ever (1 John 2:17).

teen.open: Can you be close to the world and close to Yahweh at once? Not to the world-system that runs without Him. You can love people, but your heart cannot belong to both.
teen.close: So the answer is no neutral middle. Love people, not the system. When your heart gets divided, draw near to Him, and He gives more grace.

senior.open: The title asks whether a person can be close to the world and still close to Yahweh. James and John answer plainly: friendship with the world-system is enmity with Him, though we are still called to live among and love its people.
senior.close: So the answer stands. In the world, not of it: present among people, with affection set on things above. The world passes away; the one who does His will abides for ever.

ea-gh-suppress-the-truth.reason: The why (holding truth down is suppression, not ignorance; refusing to honor and thank Him darkens the heart) is spread through middle sections; ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-suppress-the-truth.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does suppressing what is plainly seen darken the mind? Because the problem is never a lack of evidence. Creation shows His eternal power, and the conscience knows it. When a person holds that truth down instead of honoring and thanking Him, the mind does not stay neutral: imaginations go vain, the heart is darkened, and in the end Yahweh gives them over to what they chose (Romans 1:21, 28). Here is how Paul traces it.
ea-gh-suppress-the-truth.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does suppressing what is plainly seen darken the mind? Because suppression is work done against the light. The evidence stays on the table; only the one pushing it down changes, step by step, from unthankful to vain to darkened. The same move made on plain facts darkens us in the same way. The way out is willingness and confession: let the truth come up, name what is clearly seen, and give thanks. The truth received makes you free (John 8:32), and the thankful mind keeps the window open to the light.

teen.open: Why does pushing down a truth you can plainly see make your mind darker? Because the truth does not go away. You change. Not thanking Him, and not admitting what you know, slowly dims your heart.
teen.close: So holding down the truth darkens the one who does it. Let it come up instead. Admit it, thank Yahweh, and the truth will set you free.

senior.open: The title asks why suppressing the plainly seen darkens the mind. Paul answers that the failure is not ignorance but holding truth down; refusing to glorify Him and give thanks leads to vain imaginings and a darkened heart.
senior.close: So suppression darkens the one who practices it, while the evidence remains. Confession reverses it: letting the truth rise, naming it precisely, and keeping a thankful heart.

ea-gh-appointed-day-ordained-judge.reason: First section states it (a day appointed, Jesus the Judge, the resurrection as proof), but the lesson ends on discussion prompts rather than landing the empty tomb as the assurance.
ea-gh-appointed-day-ordained-judge.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Acts 17:31 reveal about the empty tomb and the Judge Yahweh named? That the day of judgment is already fixed, that the Judge is Jesus, and that Yahweh raised Him from the dead as public proof to all men. The empty tomb is heaven's notice of the court date. Here is how the apostles preached it.
ea-gh-appointed-day-ordained-judge.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does Acts 17:31 reveal? The court date is already on the calendar: Yahweh has appointed a day to judge the world in righteousness, He has named the Judge, Jesus, and He sealed both by raising Him from the dead. That same risen Judge offers remission of sins to whoever believes in His name (Acts 10:43). So you live ready, you speak both the warning and the welcome, and you rest in the empty tomb as a guarantee nobody can repeal.

teen.open: What does Acts 17:31 tell us? Yahweh has set a day to judge the world, Jesus is the Judge, and raising Him from the dead is the proof.
teen.close: So the date is set and the Judge is Jesus. The empty tomb proves it, and the same Jesus forgives everyone who believes in Him.

senior.open: Acts 17:31 reveals three things: a day already appointed, a Judge already named, and the resurrection of Jesus given as assurance to all men.
senior.close: So the empty tomb is the guarantee. The day is real, the Judge is real, and the remission offered through His name is real; we live ready and tell others both.

ea-gh-judgment-seat-of-christ.reason: States all must appear early, but what readiness means (labour to be accepted, keep your own account current, leave your brother's file to the Son) only comes in the last third; ends on prompts.
ea-gh-judgment-seat-of-christ.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Will you be ready when every account is read? Every believer will appear before the judgment seat of Christ. It is not condemnation but the Son reviewing His family's stewardship. You are ready when you live toward that seat now: labouring to be accepted of Him, working heartily as to the Lord, and keeping your own account current instead of auditing your brother's. Here is how Paul teaches it.
ea-gh-judgment-seat-of-christ.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Will you be ready when every account is read? You will be, if you live toward that seat today. The foundation is Christ, and it holds; what you build on it will be tested. So labour to be accepted, do whatever you do heartily as to the Lord, keep short accounts with the Judge, and leave your brother's case file in Jesus' hands. You have one docket you can do something about, your own. Tend it, and you can meet Him with confidence, not shame (1 John 2:28), and hear, well done, thou good and faithful servant.

teen.open: Will you be ready when Jesus reviews your life? Every believer will stand before Him. You get ready by living for Him now and taking care of your own choices, not judging other people's.
teen.close: So you get ready today. Work for Jesus with your whole heart, keep your own record clean with Him, and leave other people's records to Him.

senior.open: The title asks whether we will be ready when every account is read. Paul teaches that all believers will appear before the judgment seat of Christ, a review of stewardship rather than condemnation, and that readiness is a life laboured toward His acceptance.
senior.close: So readiness is not anxiety but faithfulness. Keep your own account current, work heartily as unto the Lord, leave your brother's account with the Son, and look for confidence at His appearing.

ea-gh-vacate-the-seat.reason: Answers early (one Lawgiver; the Father committed all judgment to the Son), but ends on discussion prompts after WHAT CHANGES rather than landing who sits in the chair.
ea-gh-vacate-the-seat.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who gets to sit in the judge's chair? Not you, and not me. There is one Lawgiver, and the Father has committed all judgment to the Son. You may discern fruit and restore a brother gently, but passing final verdict on a soul is sitting in His chair without His commission. Here is how the Word hands the verdict back to Him.
ea-gh-vacate-the-seat.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who gets to sit in the judge's chair? The Son, and only the Son. The seat is occupied by covenant, and the time is His too: judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come (1 Corinthians 4:5). So you discern fruit, speak truth and restore gently, but you hand every final verdict to its actual Judge. That is not pretending the wrong did not matter. It is trusting the right Judge with perfect knowledge and perfect justice, and it sets you free from cases you were never assigned.

teen.open: Who gets to be the judge of other people's souls? Only Jesus. You can tell right from wrong, but you do not get to decide that someone is beyond Yahweh's reach.
teen.close: So the judge's chair belongs to Jesus. Hand Him the people you want to condemn. You will feel lighter, and He will handle it rightly.

senior.open: The title asks who may sit in the judge's chair. James and Paul answer plainly: there is one Lawgiver, and the Father has committed all judgment to the Son. Our part is discernment and gentle restoration, not final verdicts.
senior.close: So the chair is the Son's. Vacating it does not excuse wrong; it entrusts the case to the right Judge at the right time, and it frees the heart from bitterness it was never meant to carry.

ea-gh-testing-not-temptation.reason: First section answers it (temptation never comes from Yahweh; testing does and grows character), but the lesson ends on discussion prompts instead of the answer and the built-in exit.
ea-gh-testing-not-temptation.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is temptation ever Yahweh's doing? No. Temptation is a pull toward sin, drawn out of our own desire and exploited by the adversary, and Yahweh tempts no one (James 1:13-14). Testing is different: He uses trials to grow character, never designed for you to fail. And in both, He has already built the way of escape. Here is how to tell bait from a test.
ea-gh-testing-not-temptation.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is temptation ever Yahweh's doing? Never. Bait toward sin comes from our own desire; a test that grows you comes from His hand, and every good gift comes from the Father of lights. So when pressure hits, ask which it is. Resist the bait and look for the exit He built before it arrived. Endure the test and read it as a mirror and a doorway. Either way, Yahweh is faithful: He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear (1 Corinthians 10:13).

teen.open: Does Yahweh ever tempt you to sin? Never. Temptation comes from your own wants. A test is different; He uses it to make you stronger.
teen.close: So temptation is never from Him. Resist the bait and take the way out He already made. Stick with the test, because it is growing you.

senior.open: The title asks whether temptation is ever Yahweh's doing. James answers no: temptation comes from our own desire, while testing is His way of growing character, and He provides the way of escape in both.
senior.close: So we stop blaming Him for temptation and stop reading every hardship as punishment. Resist the one, endure the other, and find Him faithful in both.

ea-gh-all-things-work-together.reason: Opening sections answer it (not all things are good, but all are woven toward the good of conforming us to the Son), yet the lesson ends on discussion prompts, not the settled outcome.
ea-gh-all-things-work-together.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does a hard season have a rigged ending? For those who love Yahweh and are called according to His purpose, yes. Romans 8:28 does not say every thing is good; some things are plainly evil. It says He weaves all of them together for good, and the good is being conformed to the image of His Son. The outcome is settled before the trial arrives. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-all-things-work-together.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does a hard season have a rigged ending? It does, in your favour, if you love Him. Joseph's brothers meant it for evil, and Yahweh meant it for good (Genesis 50:20). Paul's chains carried the gospel into the palace. The threads can be dark, but the Weaver is never surprised, and the end He is working is your likeness to His Son and your glory with Him. So you grieve honestly and endure faithfully, facing the trial as someone the outcome already favours, because nothing can separate you from His love (Romans 8:38-39).

teen.open: Does a hard time have a good ending already set? If you love Yahweh, yes. Not everything is good, but He weaves it all together for your good.
teen.close: So the ending is already secured. Like Joseph, you may not see it yet, but He is working it for good. You can face the hard thing with confidence.

senior.open: The title asks whether a hard season has a settled ending. Romans 8:28 answers yes for those who love Yahweh: not that all things are good, but that He works them together for the good of conforming us to His Son.
senior.close: So the outcome is not in question. As with Joseph and with Paul, the evil is real and the good is greater; we may weep for a night, but we endure knowing joy comes in the morning.

ea-gh-god-beyond-dimension.reason: Opening sections answer it (He is not far up but beyond our dimension, holding it, and so near), but the lesson closes on discussion prompts rather than the answer.
ea-gh-god-beyond-dimension.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is reality bigger than your ceiling? Yes, far bigger. Yahweh is not someone far up past the sky. He is beyond our dimension, outside the frame and holding it, for by Him all things consist (Colossians 1:17). Because He holds the frame, He is also nearer than the room you are sitting in. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-god-beyond-dimension.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is reality bigger than your ceiling? It is. The One who framed the worlds holds every dimension He made, moves freely within it, as when the Spirit caught Philip away to Azotus, and still dwells with the humble. The smallness is ours, not His. So stop shrinking Him to a place or a physics you can measure. Pray to One who is not far away, hold your own certainties humbly, and face what looks impossible with Yahweh's own question in mind: is any thing too hard for the LORD? (Genesis 18:14).

teen.open: Is reality bigger than what you can see or measure? Yes. Yahweh is not just far up in the sky. He made the whole frame of the world and holds it together, so He is close too.
teen.close: So reality is much bigger than your ceiling. Jesus holds everything together, and He is near you right now. Nothing is too hard for Him.

senior.open: The title asks whether reality is larger than our ceiling. Colossians answers that by the Son all things were created and consist; Yahweh is not distant in space but beyond our dimension, holding it, and therefore present everywhere within it.
senior.close: So the felt distance of Yahweh is our limitation, not His absence. He frames and holds all things, and we worship Him with awe and pray to Him as One who is near.

ea-gh-fruit-no-law.reason: First section answers it (works are manufactured, fruit is grown from the connection, not willpower) and the root-not-branch section deepens it, but the lesson ends on prompts.
ea-gh-fruit-no-law.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How does Yahweh's Spirit grow fruit instead of forcing effort? The flesh has works, made by effort; the Spirit has fruit, grown where you stay connected. You walk in the Spirit and abide in the Vine, and love, joy, peace and the rest grow from that root (John 15:4). No law forbids that life, because every law was reaching for it. Here is how Paul teaches it.
ea-gh-fruit-no-law.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How does the Spirit grow fruit instead of forcing effort? By connection, not by willpower. When a fruit is missing, white-knuckling the branch is flesh-work in fruit's clothing; you fix the root and reconnect to the Vine. Walk in the Spirit, be led of Him, abide, and the one fruit grows over time, love fulfilling all the law was reaching for. That is a life no law forbids and no court can prosecute, and it keeps bearing fruit even in old age (Psalm 92:14).

teen.open: How does the Holy Spirit make you good without you forcing it? Fruit grows on a tree; it is not made in a factory. Stay close to Jesus, and the fruit grows.
teen.close: So you do not grit your teeth to be good. You stay connected to Jesus, the Vine, and the Holy Spirit grows love, joy and peace in you. No law can stop that.

senior.open: The title promises a life no law can forbid. Paul's answer is that the flesh produces works by effort, while the Spirit grows fruit in those who walk with Him and abide in the Vine.
senior.close: So the remedy for a missing virtue is the root, not the branch. Walk in the Spirit and abide in Christ, and the fruit grows and remains, even into old age.

ea-gh-triumph-already-public.reason: Builds the finished triumph for most of the lesson; the answer to why not study the enemy (you announce a settled verdict; attention is formative) only comes in a late section. Ends on prompts.
ea-gh-triumph-already-public.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why study a defeated enemy? You do not need to. At the cross Jesus spoiled principalities and powers and made a public show of them (Colossians 2:15). The verdict is already handed down. You do not research a defeated party to beat it again; you stand in the victory and announce the judgment that stands, keeping your eyes on Jesus. Here is how the Word shows the triumph is finished.
ea-gh-triumph-already-public.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why study a defeated enemy? Because you do not have to win what is already won. The weapons are stripped, the charge against you is nailed to the cross, and the Son is seated waiting for His enemies to become His footstool. Staring at the darkness only makes you anxious and fascinated by it; attention forms you. So set your mind on things above and look unto Jesus. When fear, temptation or accusation comes, you stand on the victory He already won and say so. You enforce a verdict; you do not fight for one.

teen.open: Why should you not spend your time studying the enemy? Because Jesus already beat him at the cross. The fight is over. Your job is to stand in what Jesus won.
teen.close: So keep your eyes on Jesus, not on the darkness. When fear or guilt shows up, remember: the verdict is already in, and Jesus won.

senior.open: The title asks why anyone should study a defeated enemy. Colossians 2:15 answers that the contest was settled at the cross, so believers do not research the adversary but stand in a finished victory.
senior.close: So we fix our attention on the risen Son, not the darkness He stripped. Accusation has nothing left to hold, and we live by enforcing a verdict rather than fighting for one.

ea-gh-will-worship-frees-no-one.reason: First section answers it (rules have a show of wisdom but no power against the flesh), and THE PERSON WHO FREES completes it, but the lesson ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-will-worship-frees-no-one.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can rules that look holy still change nothing? Yes. Colossians 2:23 admits man-made rules have a show of wisdom, humility and discipline, then judges them by their yield: they do not restrain the flesh. They look like power and produce none. Freedom comes from a Person, Jesus, not from a procedure. Here is how Paul measures it.
ea-gh-will-worship-frees-no-one.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Looks holy, changes nothing? That is the Word's own verdict on rules detached from Christ. You can count the fasts, the steps and the prohibitions, but the Word measures by yield, not appearance, and the yield is nothing against the flesh. What the law could not do, Yahweh did by sending His Son. So when a checklist promises freedom, ask whether it gives the yield or only the show. Then come to the Head Himself, because if the Son makes you free, you are free indeed (John 8:36), and His grace actually teaches you to live godly.

teen.open: Can rules look holy and still not change you? Yes. Paul says rules people make up look wise, but they cannot stop sin inside you. Only Jesus can set you free.
teen.close: So do not trust a checklist to fix you. Come to Jesus. When He sets you free, you are really free, and His grace changes you from the inside.

senior.open: The title asks whether practices can look holy and change nothing. Colossians 2:23 says exactly that: man-made rules have a show of wisdom but no power against the flesh.
senior.close: So we judge every system by its yield, not its appearance, and return to Christ, the Head. Freedom is a Person, and His grace does what rules never could.

ea-gh-jesus-i-know-who-are-ye.reason: Second section answers it (right name, no relationship; standing is being known by Him), and later sections build it, but the lesson ends on discussion prompts, not the answer.
ea-gh-jesus-i-know-who-are-ye.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why is using the right name not enough? The sons of Sceva named Jesus and cited Paul, and still fled wounded. They knew about Jesus, but He did not know them. Real standing before Yahweh is not a correct formula; it is being known by Him, a living relationship with the One whose name you speak. Here is what Acts 19 reveals.
ea-gh-jesus-i-know-who-are-ye.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why is the right name not enough? Because the name of Jesus is not a spell; it is the name of a Person, and it works for those He knows. The spirit said it plainly: Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye? Peter and John had no credentials, yet the council saw they had been with Jesus. So the question before you speak is not, do I have the right words, but, does He know me? For every true believer the answer is a sweet yes, and that standing grows by walking with Him in His Word, prayer, obedience and love.

teen.open: Is saying the name of Jesus enough? The sons of Sceva said it and still got beaten. They knew about Jesus, but they did not know Him. What matters is being known by Him.
teen.close: So it is not about using the right words. It is about knowing Jesus and being known by Him. Spend time with Him, and His name becomes yours to speak.

senior.open: The title says using the right name is not enough. Acts 19 shows why: the sons of Sceva had the formula but not the relationship, and real standing is being known by Yahweh.
senior.close: So spiritual authority is not collected like phrases. It grows from walking with Jesus, and the Lord knows them that are His; that is the standing that matters.

ea-gh-submit-then-resist.reason: THE MIDDLE TERM answers early (resistance framed by submission carries His weight; alone it is shouting), and WHAT CHANGES restates it, but the lesson ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-submit-then-resist.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does James 4:7-8 put nearness to Yahweh before your resistance? Because resistance alone is a man shouting at an enemy with nothing behind him. Submit to Yahweh, resist the devil, draw near to Yahweh: resistance is the middle term, framed on both sides by nearness. Surrender first is what gives your resisting His weight, and that is when the promise holds, he will flee from you. Here is how the Word sets the order.
ea-gh-submit-then-resist.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does James put nearness before resistance? Because the order is the instruction. Peter gives the same order, and Jesus lived it: a submitted Son answering the tempter with it is written. Most failed resisting is the right words in the wrong sequence, shouting at the darkness while holding the very pride or bitterness that gives it a foothold. So lead with surrender, not confrontation: bow first, then resist on His Word, then draw near again. Then the adversary flees, and the better promise follows: Yahweh draws near to you (James 4:8).

teen.open: Why does James say to give yourself to Yahweh before you fight back against the devil? Because fighting back alone has no power. Being close to Yahweh is what makes it work.
teen.close: So bow first, then push back. Give yourself to Yahweh, stand on His Word, and draw close to Him. The devil flees, and Yahweh comes near.

senior.open: The title asks why James places nearness to Yahweh before resistance. The answer is in his order: submission and drawing near frame resistance on both sides, and that is what gives it weight.
senior.close: So we lead with surrender rather than confrontation. Humbled before Him we receive more grace, resist on His Word, and find that He draws near to us.

ea-gh-not-bondage-again.reason: The son-versus-servant difference (a son's place is permanent; a son cries Abba, a slave checks if he is still allowed in) is spread through the middle; ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-not-bondage-again.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What is the difference between a son and a servant at Yahweh's door? A servant's place in the house is always provisional, so he keeps checking whether he is still allowed in. A son's place is permanent, so he cries Abba, Father, and comes in boldly. In Christ you have received the Spirit of adoption, not a spirit of bondage again to fear (Romans 8:15). Here is how Paul shows it.
ea-gh-not-bondage-again.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why stop flinching at Yahweh's door? Because you are a son, not a servant. The yoke was broken when He sent His Son to redeem you, and fear sneaks back only as anxious carefulness. Listen to your cry: a son says Abba; a slave checks the door. The prodigal came home rehearsing a servant's speech, and the father ran to him and put a son's robe, ring and shoes on him. So stand fast in that liberty (Galatians 5:1). Obedience, repentance and holiness all remain, but they flow from love, not dread. You are in.

teen.open: Do you still feel nervous about whether Yahweh will let you in? If you belong to Jesus, you are His child, not a hired servant. Children do not have to keep checking if they are allowed home.
teen.close: So stop flinching. Like the son the father ran to, you are welcomed as family. Call Him Father, and come in with confidence.

senior.open: The title asks about still flinching at Yahweh's door. Paul's answer is that believers have received the Spirit of adoption: a servant's place is provisional, a son's is permanent, and a son draws near crying Abba, Father.
senior.close: So we hold our freedom as sons rather than renting it as servants. Obedience and repentance remain, but they run toward the Father in love, not away from Him in dread.

ea-gh-keep-yourself-by-the-word.reason: Opens by naming the daily decision, but how it keeps you growing (line upon line, stored in the heart, both hands, doing it the same day) is spread across later sections; ends on prompts.
ea-gh-keep-yourself-by-the-word.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How does daily obedience to Yahweh's Word keep you growing? Not through one big decision, but through small ones repeated: take in a line, store it in your heart, do it the same day, and take the next line. Two hands hold you as you go: you keep yourself in His love, and He is able to keep you from falling (Jude 1:21, 24). Here is how the Word teaches it.
ea-gh-keep-yourself-by-the-word.example: ONE LINE, ONE DAY. Say you read Psalm 119:11 on a Monday morning and store that one verse in your heart. That afternoon a sharp word rises in you, and the verse you loaded is there to consult. You do what it says and hold your tongue. Tuesday you take the next line. Nothing dramatic happened, yet the loop closed the same day, and a sense was exercised by use.
ea-gh-keep-yourself-by-the-word.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How does daily obedience keep you growing? One small step at a time, the way Yahweh teaches: precept upon precept, line upon line. You hide the Word in you, not just near you, and you close the loop by doing what you read the same day, because understanding is not obedience. Big resolutions collapse because they run on willpower; this walk runs on faithfulness in small things, held by two hands, one of which never tires. And it compounds: the path of the just shines more and more unto the perfect day (Proverbs 4:18).

teen.open: How do you keep growing with Yahweh? Not by one huge decision, but by small daily steps. Read a little of His Word, remember it, and do it.
teen.close: So take one line at a time and do it today. You hold on, and Yahweh holds you too. Bit by bit, your light grows brighter.

senior.open: The title contrasts one big decision with one small step. The Word teaches that growth comes line upon line: a little received, stored in the heart, and obeyed the same day, held both by our hand and His.
senior.close: So the walk is a direction, not a sudden arrival. Small obediences repeated train the senses, and we rest because the One able to keep us from falling holds the other hand.

ea-gh-word-is-4d-fact.reason: First section answers it (Scripture inverts the ranking: the unseen and eternal Word goes first), and the four tests prove it, but the lesson ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-word-is-4d-fact.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. When data and Scripture seem to clash, which witness goes first? The Word. The things which are seen are temporal; the things which are not seen are eternal (2 Corinthians 4:18). Yahweh's Word outranks on every test we already use for evidence: it lasts, it does not change, its Witness cannot lie, and our instrument is the dim one. Real data still stays real. Here is how to hold both.
ea-gh-word-is-4d-fact.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Which witness goes first when data and Scripture seem to clash? His Word, every time, and decided before the clash comes. It stands for ever while grass withers (Isaiah 40:8); it is settled in heaven; let Yahweh be true, but every man a liar (Romans 3:4). That does not make measurement worthless: He made what we measure, so verify your data rigorously. But when a reading seems to overturn a settled Word, the part more likely to be partial is ours. Hold the Word, keep working, and expect the two to agree in time, because they share one Author.

teen.open: When something you see seems to argue with the Bible, which one do you trust first? Yahweh's Word. What you see lasts a while; His Word lasts for ever, and He cannot lie.
teen.close: So put His Word first, and still check facts carefully. If they do not fit yet, our view is the limited one. In time they will agree, because Yahweh made both.

senior.open: The title asks which witness goes first when data and Scripture appear to conflict. Paul, Isaiah and Romans answer the Word: it is eternal, settled, spoken by One who cannot lie, while our instruments see through a glass darkly.
senior.close: So we rank His Word first while honouring real data. When they cannot yet be reconciled, we hold the Word and keep working, expecting agreement, for one Author made both.
